title: First trimester pregnancy screening
what: An ultrasound of the baby at 11 to 13 weeks plus a blood test for the mother. Together they check how the baby is growing and the chance of some chromosome conditions.
why: Offered to all pregnant women at 11 to 13 weeks.
duration: the ultrasound usually takes 20 to 30 minutes, plus a blood test
tell_doctor: The exact date of your last period
If the pregnancy is from IVF

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: Strictly between 11 weeks and 13 weeks and 6 days. After that, this screening is no longer done.

prepare.title: Bladder
prepare.text: Ask your clinic. Sometimes you are asked to come with a full bladder, sometimes the opposite.

prepare.title: Blood test
prepare.text: The blood test is usually done on the same day, or 1 to 2 days before the ultrasound, as the lab requires.

steps: You lie on your back with your belly uncovered
The doctor puts on gel and looks at the baby through your belly
The baby's size, heartbeat, and the fluid at the back of the neck are measured
Sometimes a vaginal probe is used for more accuracy
Blood is taken from a vein, if not done yet
feel: It does not hurt. You will feel the probe pressing
You can see your baby on the screen and hear the heartbeat
after: A program calculates the risks from the ultrasound and blood test. Results come in a few days
A high risk is not a diagnosis. The doctor will explain which follow-up tests are needed
red_flags: Bleeding or pain low in the belly: see a doctor without waiting for the screening

faq.q: Is ultrasound harmful to the baby?
faq.a: No. Ultrasound has been widely used in pregnancy for a long time, and it has no radiation.

reminders.text: First trimester screening tomorrow. Check if you need a full bladder, and bring your pregnancy record.
